newsitem.title: USA: Ex-ADM executive pleads guilty to fraud.
newsitem.headline: Ex-ADM executive pleads guilty to fraud.

text.p: A former Archer Daniels Midland Co executive has pleaded guilty to a conspiracy charge to commit fraud and transmit checks taken by fraud in interstate commerce, the U.S. Justice Department said Wednesday.
It said Marty Allison, 39, who had been vice president of ADM's BioProducts division, entered the guilty plea on Tuesday at a hearing in federal court in Chicago.

According to court documents, Allison from the fall of 1991 through September of 1995 conspired with others to illegally obtain money and property from ADM, the department said. It said sentencing in the case has yet to be scheduled.
The case stemmed from an investigation conducted by the FBI in Chicago and the Internal Revenue Service. The prosecution was handled by the Justice Department's fraud unit.
Allison became the third person charged in the probe.

The department three weeks ago said Reinhard Richter, another former vice-president at the BioProducts division, had been charged in an eight-count indictment with submitting false invoices to steal more than $180,000 from the company.

Mark Whitacre, the former president of ADM's BioProducts division, was charged last month in a 45-count indictment alleging he embezzled more than $9 million from the company, filed false tax returns and later sought to obstruct the government's investigation.
